objective: Use numeric accumulator inference and a for-of traversal to sum existing UTF-16 string lengths.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Type inference and string.length remain current language foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Summing lengths is a small practical aggregation with an explicit unit.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Accumulator inference transfers to other typed loops.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Minimal annotations and a for-of loop fit an introductory TypeScript objective.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: The bounded exercise prevents text-unit confusion but has limited operational risk.

defects: Junior used an indexed loop and senior reduce despite the requested for-of teaching example.
Unicode length units, dense/frozen domain and cost variable were unstated.
A code-point counter passed every ASCII-only assertion.
rationale: Retain the correct reference and align both model boards with for-of plus an inferred accumulator. Define up to 1000 ordinary strings of 1000 UTF-16 units, nonmutation and existing length access rather than grapheme counting. Tests distinguish emoji, combining sequence and lone surrogate lengths, spaces/newline/empty strings, and 1000 maximal words. Author O(n) in word count because reading .length does not scan a string. The TypeScript static checker and runtime runner are distinct; no claim that inference adds runtime validation or that the grader enforces a particular loop syntax.

objective: Connect generic input and output element types while forwarding exactly one callback argument per item.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Generic callbacks and collection transforms remain current TypeScript foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Typed array transformations are common application data work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Separating input and callback result types transfers to higher-order APIs.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Two generic parameters and one callback form a bounded foundational exercise.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Extra callback arguments or lost value/type identity cause subtle API bugs.

defects: Senior Array.from(items, change) passed its index despite the one-argument contract.
Exact result identity, fresh output, throw propagation and callback order were unverified.
A direct items.map(change) implementation passed all previous tests.
Existing positive result assignments did not reject an unrelated output type.
rationale: Wrap the senior callback so Array.from forwards only item; retain correct reference/junior. Define dense/frozen up-to-1000 inputs, no callback mutation, synchronous ordered calls and fresh mutable dense output. Preserve opaque values including native Promises without awaiting; forward the exact synchronous throw and stop later calls. Four new runtime cases cover arity/order, opaque identity/fresh output, Symbol failure cutoff and 1000 calls. Hidden type checks accept structured objects and Promise results and reject string[] from a numeric callback result. O(n) wrapper/result cost excludes callback work.

objective: Produce a stable round-robin service sequence without treating an empty string as an empty queue.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Typed arrays, optional returns and round-robin traversal remain current foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Queue simulations are useful for allocation and scheduling exercises.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Checking absence rather than falsiness transfers to other optional-return APIs.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The copied shift/push teaching form makes string-or-undefined visible to beginners.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: The exercise prevents basic ordering and missing-value bugs, rather than specifying a production scheduler.

defects: Prompt required a copied queue although correct junior/senior implementations used nonmutating indexed access.
Name/turn bounds, empty-name behavior and fresh outputs were unstated.
A falsiness check on shifted names passed all prior tests.
No cost guidance distinguished repeated shifts from indexed cycling.
rationale: Keep all three correct boards and explain that copied shift/push is the teaching approach while equivalent indexed cycles are valid. Bound strings/1000 entries and integer turns0..10000; preserve duplicate/empty/Unicode names and fresh results without changing waiting. Tests cover empty-string entries, independent repeated/zero/empty results and 10000 outputs from a frozen 1000-entry queue. Author O(n²) as a deliberately stated worst-case upper bound for the taught shift approach under linear shift, with n=1+w+t; include the more precise O(w+t*w), retained O(w+t), and explain that indexing can be faster. This does not falsely label the original repeated shift linear or enforce the slower method on alternatives.

objective: Find a finite numeric range with one traversal and an exact fresh two-position tuple.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Numeric comparisons and tuple result typing remain current TypeScript fundamentals.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Ranges are useful in charting, validation and small aggregate calculations.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Seeded extrema and a single pass transfer to other numeric summaries.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A finite bounded numeric list and explicit empty result fit a foundational task.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Sorting/mutating source data or fabricating a zero extremum changes real results.

defects: Junior sorted a copied list despite the required single pass.
Senior Math.min/Math.max chose signed-zero ties differently from reference comparisons.
Finite domain, nonmutation, fresh result and tie policy were unstated.
Sorting the original input passed all previous assertions.
rationale: Keep reference and replace junior/senior with single-pass comparisons. Define at most10000 finite bounded numbers, read-only/frozen input, earliest tied value including zero sign, fresh mutable [low, high] and fresh [0,0] on empty. Cases reject sorting/mutation, inspect fractional extremes and unchanged order, preserve signed-zero ties and check 10000 values at domain bounds. Existing type cases protect exact tuple width/number entries. Author O(n) time and O(1) retained state besides output; no sorting assumption or NaN ordering policy is invented.

objective: Swap opaque tuple entries and their separate generic types while returning a fresh pair.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Generic tuple positions and destructuring remain current TypeScript syntax.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: The small pair transformation has narrow direct utility but supports typed API work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Position-preserving generic relationships transfer to tuple-based functions.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Two opaque entries make a clear introductory destructuring exercise.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: It prevents basic aliasing/type-position mistakes in this limited operation.

defects: Junior indexed a parameter instead of the expressly requested parameter destructuring.
Opaque identity, signed zero and frozen inputs were unverified.
Cloning both entries with JSON passed all previous structural comparisons.
rationale: Retain reference and correct readonly-capable senior; align junior to destructuring the annotated parameter tuple. Define opaque entries, exact identity and fresh mutable pair per call, including equal references and frozen input. Tests distinguish original frozen record/array references, functions/Symbols/undefined/NaN/-0 and independent outputs. Additional type checks preserve exact literal slots and reject the unflipped generic result. Target constant time/output regardless of nested entry size: nothing traverses opaque values. The public mutable tuple signature is retained; readonly static acceptance is not newly required merely because runtime inputs may be frozen.
